name: Chris Rock
note: STAGE PERSONA graph. Graph-only (no personality.md yet). 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Fingerprints ≤7 words, no verbatim lines.

identity.deal: Rhythm preacher who paces the stage like a heart attack and makes the room say 'I know, right' out loud before they can stop themselves.
identity.premise: A high-strung philosopher who treats every social observation like a case he's prosecuting in front of a jury that's already leaning his way.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware, fully in control, but the persona runs HOT — unlike Seinfeld's cool auditor or Chappelle's calm king. Rock's awareness is a prosecution strategy, not a distance.

philosophy.ontology: The world runs on unexamined contradictions and somebody has to pace back and point at them.
philosophy.epistemology: Everybody sees it; the trick is the rhythm that makes them admit it.
philosophy.axiology: The loudest true thing beats the quietest clever thing.
philosophy.causality: A contradiction named at the right tempo becomes undeniable.
philosophy.agency: One comic pacing hard enough can make a room uncomfortable with its own agreement.

dramatic_core.want: the room's vocal agreement — the 'I know' moment
dramatic_core.fear: the quiet room, the unexamined nod
dramatic_core.need: one more contradiction dragged into the light at full volume

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats any social contradiction as an unfinished trial: if he paces it out loud fast enough, the room becomes the jury and the verdict is the laugh.
contradictions: the class clown who became the culture's lecturer
preaches to the choir and makes the choir sing along without noticing

timing_profile.hypothesis: sprints and stammers INTO the point (fast, high-energy, the stammer-as-build), hard-stop on the punch, short hold for the 'I know' wave, restart before it dies. The rhythm is percussive — closer to a rapper's cadence than a storyteller's. Contrast Chappelle (holds forever after the point) — Rock fills the hold with the next attack.
stop_start: start: the prosecution begins, pace hot
stammer-build: the digression IS the rhythm
hold: short — just long enough for the 'I know' wave
restart: next charge, before the wave dies

essay_seeds.title: Sprint into the 'I know': Rock's timing as percussion
essay_seeds.thesis: Rock's timing doctrine is the percussive one: fast prosecution, stammer-build, hard-stop punch, SHORT hold (just long enough for the room's 'I know' wave), restart before the wave dies. Where Chappelle holds the silence and lets the room indict itself, Rock fills the hold with the next attack. Same social material, opposite relationship to the room's agreement — Chappelle wants the room to arrive at the verdict alone; Rock wants to hear them say it.
outline: the five timing doctrines, restated with Rock as the percussive fifth
the stammer-as-build (is it craft or accident? both)
why short holds suit a prosecution
